# /smart-page

## Purpose

Take one scene from its breakdown to pages that are ready to generate, in a
single directed pass. The command stages the scene on its map, lays out the
pages, scripts every panel, fills and audits the ledger, picks the
references, and compiles the prompt packages. `/page-plan`,
`/panel-script`, `/panel-ledger`, and `/reference-plan` do the same work as
separate stations. Here one intent runs through all of it: the staging
explains the layout, the layout explains the framing, and the prompts are
compiled from files that already agree with each other.

## Use When

- A scene exists in `scenes/<SC_ID>.yaml` with beats and a page budget, and
  the bibles and masters it uses are approved. This is the default way to
  take a scene to pages.
- You want a complete first proposal to react to. Revise the result with
  the station commands afterwards.
- A beat was rewritten, the page budget changed, or the provider changed.
  The scene's pages are rebuilt as a set, so the plan, the ledger, and the
  prompts cannot fall out of step.

## Inputs

- `scene` (ID or path, required): the scene to realize, e.g. `SC_001_01` or
  `production/issues/ISS_001/scenes/SC_001_01.yaml`.
- `pages` (int, optional, default the page count in the scene's
  `beats[].pages`): pages to spend on the scene.
- `max_panels` (int, optional, default from the format layer): ceiling on
  panels per page.
- `provider` (string, optional, default `default_providers.image` in
  `project.yaml`): provider the reference plans and prompt packages are
  built for.
- `mode` (enum, optional, default `full_page`): `full_page` | `per_panel`,
  written to `generation.mode` of each page.

## Invokes Agents

- art-director
- layout-artist
- comic-writer
- penciller
- letterer
- continuity-editor
- prompt-director

## Required Skills

- scene-blocking
- page-layout
- sequential-storytelling
- comic-scripting
- panel-composition
- performance-direction
- state-tracking
- reference-selection
- prompt-compilation

## Process

1. Interpret the scene. Read the scene file, the story bible facts it
   adapts, the style bible, and `comic_format`. Confirm that no open
   question with `blocking: true` touches this scene. art-director states
   the scene's visual intent in one paragraph: how close the reader is kept,
   where the blacks sit, which panel the scene exists for. Later decisions
   are argued against this paragraph.
2. Block the scene. Stage it on the location map: starting positions by
   level, side, and landmark, each movement with what triggers it ("Mara
   comes down the ladder when the crates shift"), facing, and every object
   that changes hands. Confirm `geography.travel_direction` and
   `geography.threat_direction`. A position the map cannot name stops the
   command; fix it in `/location-bible`.
3. Lay out the pages. layout-artist distributes the beats, writes each
   page's `purpose`, and designs `layout.grid`, `layout.tiers`, and
   `layout.reading_order`. Each panel gets one drawable main moment in
   `moment`, a `size` that follows its weight, a `transition_in`, and an
   `ellipsis` wherever the gutter skips something on purpose. A critical
   handoff or change of level gets its own panel. Set `page_turn` and
   `side` for paged projects, and chain `continuity.enters_from` and
   `exits_to`.
4. Script the panels. comic-writer writes `background` and one `cast` row
   per visible character with `position`, `facing`, `action`, and
   `wardrobe`. A panel that only looks good and moves nothing is cut here.
5. Compose and direct. penciller completes `framing` (`shot_size`, `angle`,
   `view`, `composition`) so the actor of each moment is unmistakable, and
   writes `acting` as behavior that can be drawn. Characters listed in
   each other's `visually_adjacent_to` are staged apart and at sizes where
   their distinguishing features show.
6. Write the lettering text. letterer fills `lettering` per panel: `id`,
   `type`, `speaker`, the exact `text`, and `order`. Speakers are in the
   panel's `cast`, word counts stay inside the project's limits, and each
   panel keeps a clear area for its balloons. No caption explains an action
   the drawing does not show.
7. Fill and audit the ledger. continuity-editor walks the scene in reading
   order from the state the previous scene or issue left: rows for
   off-panel characters whose state matters, `state` and `state_changes`,
   `holding`, `carrying`, `props`, `transfers`, `moved`. Run `node
   scripts/check-continuity.js --root production --issue <ISS_ID>` and fix
   every error in the plan until it reports zero. Errors are fixed, never
   waived.
8. Select references. Fill `references.required` and `references.optional`
   in each page, then run `node scripts/build-reference-plan.js --page
   <page.yaml> --provider <id>` per page. Check the result: the look master
   with role `style`, one identity sheet per character on the page, one
   role per image. The previous page appears as `spatial_continuity` only
   once it has a reviewed render. A missing or unapproved master is a hard
   blocker: list it and stop before compiling; the fix is
   `/visual-development`.
9. Compile prompts. prompt-director runs `node scripts/compile-prompts.js
   --page <page.yaml> --provider <id>` per page. Each package carries the
   style block verbatim, the grid, each panel's moment and positions, the
   stated difference between adjacent characters, the state constraints,
   the exact `lettering_text` in `in_image` mode, and the references in
   attachment order. Set each page's `status` to `prompted`.
10. Validate and review the set. Run `node scripts/validate-workspace.js
    --root production --issue <ISS_ID>` and `node scripts/build-board.js
    --issue production/issues/<ISS_ID>`. Then run the self-evaluation gates
    on every file the command wrote, apply the clear fixes, and present the
    pages: purposes, panel counts, audit result, and blockers.

## Outputs

All under `production/issues/<ISS_ID>/`:

- `scenes/<SC_ID>.yaml`, with `pages` and `beats[].pages` updated; validates
  against `schemas/scene.schema.json`.
- `pages/<PG_ID>/page.yaml`, one per page, with layout, panel script,
  ledger, and lettering text; validates against `schemas/page.schema.json`.
- `pages/<PG_ID>/reference-plan.yaml`, validates against
  `schemas/reference-plan.schema.json`.
- `pages/<PG_ID>/prompts/<provider>.yaml`, validates against
  `schemas/prompt-package.schema.json`.
- `issue.yaml`, with `page_count`, `panel_count`, and `status` updated
  (`schemas/issue.schema.json`).
- The issue board written by `build-board.js` (HTML, no schema).

## Notes

Usage example:

```
/smart-page SC_001_01 --pages 2 --provider harness-native
```

- This command spends no generation budget. It produces the checked package
  that `/generate-pages` executes. Read the page purposes and the board
  before paying for pixels; changing a panel after a render exists costs a
  repair or a new version.
- Running it again on the same scene replaces the earlier proposal as a
  set. Old panels are never mixed with new staging. Pages that already have
  renders are not replanned without the user's decision, because their
  renders would no longer match.
- Revise with the stations: `/page-plan` for layout, `/panel-script` for
  framing and text, `/panel-ledger` after any change to who is where,
  `/reference-plan` after the manifest changes.
- Format differences: paged projects plan page turns and facing pages;
  webtoon projects plan one scroll segment per page and pace by vertical
  distance. The command reads `comic_format` first and loads one format
  layer only.
- Escalate to the user when the page budget cannot hold the beats without
  hiding a handoff, when a required master is missing, or when the staging
  needs a level or a landmark the location does not have.
- Related: `/issue-breakdown` (before), `/thumbnails` (readability test),
  `/generate-pages` (next), `/continuity-review` (audit across pages and
  issues), `/full-production` (runs this per scene).
